import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source CSV files
source_files = {
    "Source6_9_0": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_0.csv",
    "Source6_9_1": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_1.csv",
    "Source6_9_2": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_2.csv",
    "Source6_9_3": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_3.csv",
    "Source6_9_4": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_4.csv",
    "Source6_9_5": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_5.csv",
    "Source6_9_6": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_6.csv",
    "Source6_9_7": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_7.csv",
}

# Step 1: Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_9_0"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Influenced']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_9_1"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Spotify']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_9_2"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Albums in RS500']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_9_3"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Top 100 Singles', 'Highest Position']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_9_4"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Score']
df5 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_9_5"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Times on Cover of RS']
df6 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_9_6"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated']
df7 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_9_7"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Certified Units (Millions)']

# Step 2: Merge all dataframes on 'Artist' using left joins progressively
# Start from df6 because it contains multiple columns related to Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated
# This will be the "base" dimension table to join others on Artist

df_merged = df6.copy()

# Merge with df0 (Influenced)
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df0, on="Artist", how="left")

# Merge with df7 (Certified Units (Millions))
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df7, on="Artist", how="left")

# Merge with df2 (Albums in RS500)
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df2, on="Artist", how="left")

# Merge with df3 (Top 100 Singles, Highest Position)
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df3, on="Artist", how="left")

# Merge with df4 (Score)
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df4, on="Artist", how="left")

# Merge with df5 (Times on Cover of RS)
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df5, on="Artist", how="left")

# Merge with df1 (Spotify)
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df1, on="Artist", how="left")

# Step 3: Fill missing values for numeric columns with 0 or appropriate defaults
# From target examples, Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated are integers and often 0
# Other numeric columns also can be filled with 0 if missing

numeric_columns = [
    "Year Inducted",
    "Years Waited",
    "# of Years Nominated",
    "Influenced",
    "Certified Units (Millions)",
    "Albums in RS500",
    "Top 100 Singles",
    "Highest Position",
    "Times on Cover of RS",
    "Score",
    "Spotify",
]

# Fill missing numeric columns with 0 (except Score which is float, fill with 0.0)
for col in numeric_columns:
    if col in df_merged.columns:
        if col == "Score":
            df_merged[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged[col], errors='coerce').fillna(0.0)
        elif col == "Certified Units (Millions)":
            # This is float, fillna with 0.0
            df_merged[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged[col], errors='coerce').fillna(0.0)
        else:
            # Integer columns
            df_merged[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged[col], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# Step 4: Ensure the final dataframe columns are exactly as target schema and in the correct order
target_columns = [
    "Artist",
    "Year Inducted",
    "Years Waited",
    "# of Years Nominated",
    "Influenced",
    "Certified Units (Millions)",
    "Albums in RS500",
    "Top 100 Singles",
    "Highest Position",
    "Times on Cover of RS",
    "Score",
    "Spotify",
]

# Some columns might be missing if no data was found in source, add them with default values
for col in target_columns:
    if col not in df_merged.columns:
        if col == "Artist":
            # Artist must exist, but just in case
            df_merged[col] = ""
        elif col == "Score" or col == "Certified Units (Millions)":
            df_merged[col] = 0.0
        elif col == "Spotify":
            df_merged[col] = 0
        else:
            df_merged[col] = 0

# Select and reorder columns
df_final = df_merged[target_columns]

# Step 5: Export the final dataframe to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_6.csv", index_col=0)
source7 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/training_7.csv", index_col=0)

# Join all tables on 'Artist' using inner joins starting from source6 (which has the most columns)
df = source6.merge(source0, on="Artist", how="inner") \
            .merge(source7, on="Artist", how="inner") \
            .merge(source2, on="Artist", how="inner") \
            .merge(source3, on="Artist", how="inner") \
            .merge(source5, on="Artist", how="inner") \
            .merge(source4, on="Artist", how="inner") \
            .merge(source1, on="Artist", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost columns of the target schema that are string or integer and likely unique:
# ['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated']
group_by_cols = ['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated']

# Aggregate all other columns by sum (since target examples show integer/floating values that likely come from sums)
agg_dict = {
    'Influenced': 'sum',
    'Certified Units (Millions)': 'sum',
    'Albums in RS500': 'sum',
    'Top 100 Singles': 'sum',
    'Highest Position': 'sum',
    'Times on Cover of RS': 'sum',
    'Score': 'sum',
    'Spotify': 'sum'
}

df_final = df.groupby(group_by_cols, as_index=False).agg(agg_dict)

# Ensure column order matches target schema exactly
target_columns = ['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated', 'Influenced',
                  'Certified Units (Millions)', 'Albums in RS500', 'Top 100 Singles', 'Highest Position',
                  'Times on Cover of RS', 'Score', 'Spotify']

df_final = df_final[target_columns]

# Write output
df_final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_9/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
